outlines.markdown:
# The PFL Cast — Episode 1 (Week 10): Points Don't Pay Rent

**On the show:** Peyton Manning, John Madden · **Runtime:** ~11 minutes (the first episode: includes a launch intro) · **Tone:** affectionate roast

## Notes for the show writer

- **Peyton:** Has a binder for the debate itself, with tabs labeled "Wins" and "Also Wins." Dry and self-deprecating. Yells "Omaha!" whenever Madden is winning an exchange. Slips into fake commercial reads, for example for a "Win-Loss Column Premium Ledger." Can't stop teasing his "little brother" Eli about the league owner who shares the name.
- **Madden:** "BOOM!" for every big number. States the obvious like scripture ("The team with more points has more points"). Telestrator doodles of a scoreboard that keeps getting bigger. Loves McCaffrey as a tough guy. Tangents about the Madden Cruiser and turkey legs.
- **How they play off each other:** One argument runs the whole show. Madden says points are what count. Peyton says only wins count. Every segment gets dragged back to it.
- **Running bit, the Debate Scoreboard:** After each segment, Madden gives himself a "point" and Peyton gives himself a "win," and they fight over which one counts. By the end, Madden has piled up points and Peyton has more wins, and neither will concede. The scoreboard ends up as backwards as Sean's season.
- **Never say:**
  - "started," "benched," "sat," or "starting lineup." The scoring lineup fills itself from the best scorers.
  - Waivers, FAAB or projections. Roster moves are IR moves, supplemental moves and trades.
  - Any Week 11 result. Week 11 has not been played.
  - Any number not in the digest. Talk around it instead.
  - "Commissioner" for Joe. He is the league's scorekeeper.
  - Preseason or draft grades, or anything from a previous season.
  - Points against, in any wording.
  - Hypothetical or "all-play" records.
  - Anything about a defense scoring zero.
  - Busts or "nobody scored under 2."
  - Injury news. The designations reflect current status, not Week 10.
  - Made-up quotes from real owners. Describe them, never quote them.
  - Pronouns for owners. Use their names.
  - The "that's not an X, it's a Y" construction, in any wording.

## Launch intro: Welcome to The PFL Cast (~0:45)

This is the first episode ever, so open by announcing the show before the argument starts. Keep it quick and warm, and play it as a big occasion for these two.

- **Madden drives the welcome.** He makes it a grand opening: "This is the first-ever episode of The PFL Cast!" He calls in from the Madden Cruiser, or from the studio with the bus idling outside, and cuts a ribbon with a turkey leg. BOOM!
- **What the show is:** a weekly show about the PFL, the Peninsula Football League. Twelve owners, one league, every week of the season.
- **Who they are, in character:** Peyton has already prepared. He has a binder labeled "Episode 1" with tabs for every owner, and admits he's been studying for weeks. Madden admits he prepared by eating.
- **What listeners get every week:** the week's best stories (not a game-by-game recap), the awards, and each host's picks for next week. They'll come back and check the receipts on those picks.
- **The promise to the owners:** everyone gets roasted eventually, lovingly. Peyton: "If you're not mentioned this week, don't relax."
- **First disagreement before the show even starts:** they can't agree on the opening. Peyton wants a carefully rehearsed welcome. Madden has already started.
- **Handoff:** Peyton turns to the binder's first real tab, "The Argument," which leads straight into the cold open.

## 1. Cold open (~0:30)

- Peyton opens the binder to "The Argument" and announces the first episode's one topic: do points or wins matter?
- Madden: "Points! BOOM!" Peyton: wins.
- They agree to keep score of the argument itself. They immediately disagree about whether to score it in points or wins.
- **Handoff:** Peyton: "Exhibit A is Sean."

## 2. Storyline: Sean's 157.5 vs. Pete's 7-3 (~2:30)

- **Madden drives.** Sean put up 157.5, the week's high and Sean's best week of the season. Sean is still 4-6. Madden draws a giant telestrator circle around the number.
- Sean is second in the league in points, behind only Joe, and has the record of a team that loses its car keys every Sunday. Keep the roast gentle and affectionate: Sean gets this one roast and that's it.
- **Peyton counters with Pete.** Pete won with 105.5, a score that beat only 5 of the other 11 teams, and is 7-3. Peyton gives it a fake commercial read: "Pete's Team: winning without the mess of excess points."
- **The disagreement:** Madden says Pete is lucky and Sean is good. Peyton says the standings don't print "good," they print wins. Madden: "You can't eat a win." Peyton: "You can't eat a point either, John." That sets off a turkey leg tangent.
- **Scoreboard:** Madden gives himself a point and Peyton gives himself a win. Each says the other's doesn't count.
- **Handoff:** Madden: "Let me tell you about a tough guy."

## 3. Storyline: McCaffrey's 41 (~1:30)

- **Madden drives** with pure tough-guy worship. Christian McCaffrey put up 41, the week's top performance and his season high, in Chris's win over Bruce. Madden has a Cruiser story about a running back who "runs like he's late for the bus."
- **Peyton** pulls it back to the argument: Chris got a win out of it, so the win is the story.
- **The disagreement:** Madden says McCaffrey's points are the reason for the win, so points win again. Peyton: "Then it's a win. Thank you." Neither moves an inch.
- **Scoreboard:** Each claims the segment. Madden does a doodle showing that both of them won.
- **Handoff:** Peyton sighs: "Fine. Let's talk about Eli."

## 4. Storyline: Eli's best week (~1:45)

- **Peyton drives** and plays up the little-brother teasing. League owner Eli had a best-of-the-season 135.5 over Cal, with Dak Prescott at 39 and George Pickens at 33.
- Eli has now won two straight. Peyton is suspicious, flips through the binder, and treats it as a family emergency.
- **The twist:** Eli is still 3-7, so Peyton's own logic says the week barely matters. He hates admitting that.
- **The disagreement:** Madden happily takes Eli's side: "Big points, BOOM!" Peyton insists it's two wins that count, which accidentally makes his little brother look good. He yells "Omaha!" to escape.
- **Scoreboard:** Madden claims a point. Peyton reluctantly claims a win but files it under "Eli, unfortunately."
- **Handoff:** Madden: "Time for trophies!"

## 5. Awards & roast: "The Points vs. Wins Trophies" (~1:45)

Each owner gets roasted once, gently. Sean, Pete and Eli don't appear here.

- **The "Didn't Pay Rent" Award (Peyton's pick): Aaron.** Aaron lost with 114, a score that beat 6 of the other 11 teams. That's three straight losses. Peyton says it proves points don't pay rent. Madden says it proves the schedule is mean.
- **The Madden Cruiser Award for the longest trip (Madden's pick): Mike.** Mike beat Mitch by 72, the biggest margin of the week, behind Joe Burrow's 35. Madden insists Mike's points did it. Peyton notes, again, that it's one win.
- **The "One Man Band" Award: Mitch.** Mitch scored 45, a season low, and Trevor Lawrence carried most of it. Madden admires Lawrence as a tough guy hauling the whole bus up a hill. Keep it kind.
- **Honorable mention: Matt.** Matt had his worst week of the season and is still 6-3-1. Peyton loves it. Madden is offended by it.
- **Scoreboard:** They argue about whether the awards count as points or wins and settle on "both," which neither of them accepts.
- **Handoff:** Peyton: "Omaha! Picks."

## 6. Week 11 picks, with stakes (~1:30)

- **The bet that settles the show: Sean vs Chris.** Madden picks Sean, the second-highest scorer in the league. Peyton picks Chris on the record.
- **Stakes:** If Sean wins, Peyton has to read the whole binder as a turkey leg commercial. If Chris wins, Madden has to tear the scoreboard doodle off the telestrator himself.
- **Mitch vs Joe:** Mitch has the fewest points in the league and Joe has the most. Madden gives the obvious-wisdom pick. Peyton plays contrarian on principle and roots for Mitch "for the story." This is Joe's only real moment; don't force him into anything bigger.
- **Dan vs Pete:** Peyton takes Pete, who has won two straight and has the best record in the Even Division. Madden takes Dan, who has scored more points than Pete this season. This is the debate again, in miniature.
- **Mike vs Eli** as a quick-hit closer: Peyton can't bring himself to pick his "little brother," and Madden picks Eli just to annoy him.

## 7. Sign-off (~0:30)

- They read the final Debate Scoreboard. Madden leads in points, Peyton leads in wins, and both declare victory.
- Peyton realizes they've turned into Sean and Pete.
- Madden says the obvious one last time: "Whoever wins next week wins."
- Peyton closes the binder and ends on one last "Omaha!"
outlines.blurb: The points-vs-wins argument fits this week's facts perfectly, with Sean at 4-6 despite the second-most points and Pete at 7-3 winning on modest scores, and 'You can't eat a win' works; the scoreboard argument could get repetitive by segment five.
outlines.editNote: Launch intro added for the first episode (Joe, 2026-11-22)

outlines.title: The Unofficial Blowout Bowl Gala
outlines.premise: Five of the six games were decided by 48.5 or more, so the hosts throw a black-tie awards night for a week that had no drama at all. The show is a string of trophy categories: Best Supporting Running Back for McCaffrey's 41, the Lifetime Achievement in Holding the Top award for Joe and Mahomes, and the Most Gracious Loser award for Aaron, whose 114 beat 6 of the other 11 teams. Each category is set up as a nominee-and-envelope moment, and the hosts disagree on every winner.
outlines.runningBit: Madden is the gala's caterer and keeps handing a turkey leg to every winner as the actual trophy. Peyton keeps asking where the real statues are, and in the sign-off it turns out the statues were on the Madden Cruiser the whole time.
outlines.markdown:
# The PFL Cast — Week 10: The Unofficial Blowout Bowl Gala
**On the show:** Peyton Manning, John Madden · **Runtime:** ~10 minutes · **Tone:** affectionate roast

## Notes for the show writer
- **Peyton:** He is the gala's self-appointed host in a tux. He carries a binder of acceptance-speech notes no one asked for, reads fake sponsor spots between categories ("tonight's envelopes brought to you by..."), and yells "Omaha!" to cut off Madden's tangents. He keeps asking where the real statues are. He treats owner Eli's good week like a gift from heaven and still can't resist teasing his little brother.
- **Madden:** He is the gala's caterer, in an apron over his tux. He hands every winner a turkey leg as the trophy. "BOOM!" opens every envelope. He says the obvious as if it were wisdom ("the team with more points won, and that's football") and draws telestrator circles on the red carpet. He loves the tough guys and drifts into stories about the Madden Cruiser.
- **Chemistry:** Peyton wants a dignified ceremony and Madden keeps turning it into a tailgate. They disagree on every winner. Peyton argues from film, Madden argues from gut and gristle.
- **Running bit:** Each winner gets a turkey leg. Peyton asks "where are the actual statues?" and every time Madden dodges, a little more suspiciously than the last. The payoff is in the sign-off.
- **Never say:**
  - "started," "benched," "sat," "lineup decision." The scoring lineup fills itself from the best scorers.
  - waivers, FAAB, projections. Roster moves are IR, supplemental moves and trades.
  - any Week 11 result
  - any number that is not in this outline
  - "commissioner" for Joe. Joe is the scorekeeper.
  - previous seasons, draft or preseason grades
  - points scored against anyone, or "had he played everyone" records
  - "this wasn't X, it was Y" phrasing
  - made-up quotes from real owners. Describe them, never quote them.
  - he/she for owners. Use their names.
  - this week's league average (the digest figure is wrong). Also don't mention any defense that scored zero.

## 1. Cold open (~0:30)
- Peyton opens the gala doors: five of the six games were decided by 48.5 or more. It was the least dramatic week in league history, so naturally it gets a black-tie ceremony.
- Madden rolls in a cart of turkey legs. Peyton: "Those are the hors d'oeuvres?" Madden: "Those are the trophies."
- Handoff: Peyton points to the red carpet.

## 2. Red carpet (~0:45)
- Madden telestrates the arrivals and circles the "drama section." It's empty.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton says a week of blowouts is a failure of competitive balance. Madden says blowouts are honest football, because "when one guy scores more, he wins."
- Peyton's first statue question gets a mumble about "a delivery issue."
- Handoff: "Omaha! First envelope."

## 3. Best Supporting Running Back: Christian McCaffrey (~1:45)
- Driver: Peyton. Nominees are the week's big running-back days, with McCaffrey's 41 headlining. It was the top performance of the week, for Chris's win over Bruce.
- Peyton's film note: it was McCaffrey's season high by a mile. He calls it a lead role, not a supporting one.
- Madden loves McCaffrey as a tough guy who runs through people. BOOM. Turkey leg to Chris.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton says the award belongs in "Lead Actor" and the category is rigged. Madden says the category is whatever is printed on the apron.
- Light touch on Bruce as the guy in the audience clapping politely. No roast.
- Handoff: Peyton reads a fake commercial for "Envelope Insurance."

## 4. Lifetime Achievement in Holding the Top: Joe and Mahomes (~1:45)
- Driver: Madden. Joe is 7-3 and has the most points in the league, and Mahomes threw in a season-high 37 this week.
- Madden's obvious wisdom: "If you're on top, and you stay on top... you're on top."
- Peyton notes the awkwardness of giving a trophy to the scorekeeper. He asks for a recount, then remembers who does the counting.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton calls "Lifetime Achievement" premature at Week 10. Madden says that for a turkey leg, ten weeks is a lifetime.
- Second statue question. Madden says they're "parked somewhere safe."
- Handoff: Madden tears up as he introduces the next category.

## 5. Most Gracious Loser: Aaron (~1:30)
- Driver: Peyton. Aaron lost to Joe with 114, a score that beat 6 of the other 11 teams. It was the closest game of a week with no close games. That makes three straight losses for Aaron, and Aaron would have won most other matchups.
- Peyton plays it as a sad violin piece in which Aaron did everything right and drew the wrong opponent.
- **Disagreement:** Madden refuses to give a loser a turkey leg because "turkey legs are for winners." Peyton insists that grace deserves meat. Madden gives in and hands over a drumstick, a smaller trophy.
- Handoff: "Omaha! Lightning round."

## 6. Lightning-round awards (~2:00)
Quick envelopes, one roast per owner and no repeats. They disagree on each one.
- **Best Picture Nobody Saw: Sean.** Sean put up the week's high and a season best, with Gibbs and Hubbard carrying it, and is still 4-6. Peyton calls it tragic. Madden calls it beautiful.
- **Most Improved Little Brother: Eli.** It was Eli's best week, with Prescott and Pickens both setting season highs, and makes two straight wins. Peyton is visibly torn between pride and teasing Eli. Madden: "Your brother's got a real offense."
- **Best Solo Performance: Trevor Lawrence for Mitch.** Lawrence scored most of Mitch's points, which made him a one-man band. Madden hands Lawrence a turkey leg personally. Peyton wants it split with "the rest of the band." Keep it gentle.
- **Fewest Points for a Free Dinner: Pete.** Pete won with 105.5, a score that beat only 5 of the other 11 teams. Peyton admires the efficiency. Madden says a win is a win, BOOM.
- **Biggest Margin: Mike.** Mike won by 72, the week's largest margin. Madden loves the bully ball. Peyton says even blowouts need a nice ending.
- Skip Matt, Dan and Cal, or give them a brief, kind nod as "seat-fillers."
- Handoff: Peyton opens a sealed envelope marked "Week 11."

## 7. Week 11 picks, with stakes (~1:15)
- **Mitch vs Joe.** It's the fewest points in the league against the most. Madden picks Mitch as the underdog tough guy and pitches it as the upset of the gala. Peyton picks Joe and cites his binder.
- **Mike vs Eli.** Eli has won two straight. Peyton picks against his little brother "for Eli's own good." Madden picks Eli just to annoy Peyton.
- **Aaron vs Cal.** Aaron has lost three straight. Both hosts pick Aaron, and they argue about who picked him first.
- **Stakes:** The loser of the picks hands out turkey legs at next week's show, wearing the apron.

## 8. Sign-off (~0:30)
- Peyton makes one last demand for the statues. Madden opens the Madden Cruiser door and dozens of statues tumble out. They were on the bus the whole time, "riding shotgun."
- Peyton: why didn't you give those out? Madden: "You can't eat a statue."
- They close with "BOOM!" and Peyton's sponsor read for "the Madden Cruiser, now with extra trophy storage."
outlines.blurb: The statues hidden on the Cruiser are a nice payoff, but the lightning round turns into award-by-award game coverage, 'least dramatic week in league history' drags in past seasons, and 'Aaron would have won most other matchups' is a banned all-play claim.

outlines.title: Peyton Must Say It
outlines.premise: Peyton has a mission he has been dreading: to say on the air, sincerely, that his little brother Eli had a great week, with 135.5, his best of the season, two straight wins, and Dak Prescott's 39 plus George Pickens's 33. Every time he gets close he yells 'Omaha!' and swerves into another story (Sean's luckless 157.5, Joe at the top, Chris's McCaffrey day) while Madden keeps steering him back to the confession.
outlines.runningBit: Peyton's escalating stalling: a fake commercial read, a sudden deep dive in the binder, then a full film breakdown of the wrong game. Madden's telestrator literally draws the arrow back to Eli every time, and Peyton finally gets the compliment out, through gritted teeth, before the Mike vs Eli pick.
outlines.markdown:
# The PFL Cast — Week 10: Peyton Must Say It
**On the show:** Peyton Manning, John Madden · **Runtime:** ~10 minutes · **Tone:** affectionate roast

## Notes for the show writer
- **Peyton:** He has one job this episode. He has to say sincerely, on the air, that his little brother Eli had a great week. He can't do it. Play up the binder, the dry self-deprecation, the "Omaha!" swerves and the fake commercial reads. Every time he gets close to saying it, he gets visibly uncomfortable, then a little desperate, then hits a full wall. He stays likable throughout. The joke is on his pride, not on Eli.
- **Madden:** He is cheerfully relentless. Each segment, his telestrator ends in a big arrow pointing back to Eli, and he narrates the doodle while he draws it ("and this squiggle here is Peyton running away"). He states the obvious as deep wisdom ("When your brother scores a lot of points, he scored a lot of points"). He loves tough guys and drifts into turkey legs and the Madden Cruiser.
- **How they play off each other:** Peyton steers away and Madden steers back, and the stalls escalate. Segment 1 is a plain "Omaha!" swerve. Segment 2 is a fake commercial read. Segment 3 is a sudden binder deep dive that turns into a full film breakdown of the wrong game. The payoff comes just before the Mike vs Eli pick: Peyton gets the compliment out through gritted teeth, then gets oddly emotional, then denies it.
- **Running bit cue:** Every time Peyton nearly says it, he starts with "Eli had a..." and then stops.
- **Never say:**
  - "started", "benched", "sat", "lineup decision" or "should have played". There's no starting lineup in the PFL. The scoring lineup fills itself from each team's best scorers.
  - waivers, FAAB or projections. Roster moves are IR moves, supplemental moves and trades.
  - any Week 11 result. Week 11 hasn't been played.
  - any number not in the digest. If a number isn't there, talk around it.
  - "commissioner" for Joe. Joe is the scorekeeper.
  - anything about earlier seasons, preseason or draft grades.
  - points against, in any wording.
  - "all-play" or "would be X-Y against everyone" records.
  - any defense scoring zero.
  - the "that's not an X, it's a Y" construction.
  - a quote presented as coming from a real owner. Owners are only ever described.
  - a guessed pronoun for an owner. Use owners' names.
  - any roast of the same owner twice.
  - "no one scored under 2 points".

## 1. Cold open (~0:30)
- **Driver:** Madden.
- Madden announces that a mission has been handed down: Peyton has to say something nice about Eli on the air, and has to mean it.
- Peyton clears his throat, opens the binder and starts: "Eli had a..." Then he yells "Omaha!" and the theme music hits.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton claims the mission is optional. Madden says nothing is optional on the Cruiser.
- **Handoff:** Peyton swerves straight into Sean.

## 2. Sean's luckless monster week (~2:00)
- **Driver:** Peyton. He's eager to talk about anyone else.
- Sean scored 157.5, his best week of the season and the top score of the week, and beat Dan. Peyton frames it as a big score finally getting a win attached to it.
- Sean is still 4-6 despite being second in the league in points. Peyton sees heartbreak in it. Madden sees a tough guy who keeps showing up.
- Madden gushes about Gibbs and Hubbard ("two running backs, one bus"). He doesn't need to quote their numbers.
- **Disagreement:** Is Sean unlucky or cursed? Peyton has a binder tab labeled "cosmic injustice". Madden says football doesn't do curses, it does turkey legs, and nobody follows the logic.
- **Telestrator #1:** Madden circles Sean's big week and draws an arrow that keeps going off the edge of the screen and lands on Eli.
- **Handoff:** Peyton: "Eli had a..." Then "Omaha!" and a swerve to Joe.

## 3. Joe at the top (~1:45)
- **Driver:** Madden.
- Joe beat Aaron in the closest game of a blowout week, behind Mahomes's 37. Joe is 7-3 and has the most points in the league.
- Be kind to Aaron. His 114 beat 6 of the other 11 teams, and he lost anyway. Madden: "Sometimes you play great and the other guy plays more great."
- Peyton gently teases that the scorekeeper sitting on top of the scoreboard is a little suspicious. Keep it light, one beat only.
- **Stall #2:** Madden pulls out the telestrator, and Peyton bolts into a fake commercial read for a made-up product (a binder with a built-in lock "so your little brother can't read it").
- **Disagreement:** Does the closest game of the week count as a nail-biter when it was decided by 14 and a half? Peyton says yes, in this week. Madden says a nail-biter needs nails.
- **Handoff:** Madden's arrow points at Eli again. Peyton dives into the binder.

## 4. Chris's McCaffrey day (~1:45)
- **Driver:** Peyton, though he hijacks it.
- McCaffrey scored 41, the top individual performance of the week, and carried about a third of Chris's win over Bruce.
- Madden goes full tough-guy appreciation and drifts into the Cruiser: McCaffrey would get his own bunk.
- **Stall #3:** Peyton launches a frame-by-frame film breakdown with huge detail, then slowly realizes he's breaking down Mike over Mitch. It's the wrong game. Madden lets him finish before pointing it out.
- **Disagreement:** Does one player having a monster day make it a team win or a solo act? Peyton says a solo act. Madden says a team is just friends standing near a tough guy.
- **Handoff:** Madden says awards first, then Peyton owes the confession before picks.

## 5. Awards and roasts (~1:30)
- **Drivers:** They trade awards, each owner roasted once only.
- **The Good Enough Trophy, to Pete:** Pete won with a score that beat only 5 of the other 11 teams, and that's his second straight win. Peyton respects winning ugly. Madden thinks it's beautiful.
- **The Solo Act Award, to Mitch:** Trevor Lawrence did 60% of the work in Mitch's worst week of the season. Madden's doodle shows Lawrence pulling the whole bus by himself.
- **The Rough Sunday Award, to Matt:** It was Matt's worst week of the season, but Matt is still 6-3-1, so Peyton points out the record is fine. Keep it affectionate.
- **Disagreement:** Which award matters most? Peyton wants a statue. Madden wants it made of turkey.
- **Handoff:** Madden draws one last giant arrow pointing at Eli and says, "It's time."

## 6. Week 11 picks, with the confession (~2:00)
- **Drivers:** Both hosts. The stakes: the loser of the most picks has to read the other host's fake commercial next week.
- **The confession, before Mike vs Eli:** Peyton finally says it through gritted teeth. Eli scored 135.5, his best week of the season, and has two straight wins, with Dak Prescott's 39 and George Pickens's 33. Peyton gets oddly emotional, then denies being emotional. Madden says "BOOM!" and does a slow-clap telestrator heart.
- **Mike vs Eli:** Eli has won 2 straight and Mike has scored more this season. Peyton, now freed, picks Eli out of sudden loyalty. Madden picks Mike as the tough-guy rebound team. This is the episode's main disagreement.
- **Mitch vs Joe:** Most points in the league against the fewest. Madden takes the underdog "because tough guys love a fight". Peyton takes Joe because of the scorekeeper's suspicious luck. No second roast of Mitch.
- **Sean vs Chris:** A quick pick. Is this finally the week Sean's points come with a win?
- **Aaron vs Cal:** Aaron has lost 3 straight. Is the slide over? One line each.
- Keep the other games brief or skip them.
- **Handoff:** Peyton insists the confession never happened.

## 7. Sign-off (~0:30)
- **Drivers:** Both.
- Madden replays the confession on the telestrator. Peyton yells "Omaha!" over it.
- Madden signs off with a turkey leg and a "BOOM!". Peyton does a final fake commercial read promising this binder page will be destroyed.
outlines.blurb: The escalating stalls before Peyton finally says 'Eli had a...' (an Omaha swerve, then a fake binder-lock ad, then breaking down the wrong game's film) pay off with a gritted-teeth confession right before the Mike vs Eli pick.

outlines.title: The People vs. Trevor Lawrence's Back
outlines.premise: A mock courtroom where Madden, in the role of a tough-guy labor lawyer, files a workplace grievance on behalf of an overworked quarterback. Trevor Lawrence scored 27 of Mitch's 45, about 60% of the team. Peyton is the judge, ruling on whether one player carrying a team is heroism or a violation, and calls fictional expert witnesses on the other big carry jobs, such as McCaffrey's 41 for Chris and Gibbs leading Sean's 157.5. The verdict sets up Mitch vs Joe in Week 11 as the appeal.
outlines.runningBit: Exhibits keep arriving on Madden's telestrator: crude doodles of Lawrence hauling a cart with the rest of the roster riding in it, each one more elaborate. Peyton keeps sustaining objections to the drawings 'as evidence of nothing.'
outlines.markdown:
# The PFL Cast — Week 10: The People vs. Trevor Lawrence's Back
**On the show:** Peyton Manning, John Madden · **Runtime:** ~10 minutes · **Tone:** affectionate roast

## Notes for the show writer
- **Peyton Manning (the judge):** He treats the bench like a film room and brings a binder to the bench. He's dry, procedural and in love with his gavel. He yells "Omaha!" to move the court along and slips into fake commercial reads ("This recess brought to you by..."). He takes one affectionate shot at his little brother Eli, and only one.
- **John Madden (labor lawyer for the quarterback):** He's a union guy who loves tough guys, and he's outraged on behalf of the working man. Every argument is something obvious stated like it's deep wisdom ("When one guy does all the work, the other guys aren't doing the work. BOOM!"). He goes off on tangents about the Madden Cruiser and turkey legs as "evidence of what a real workload looks like."
- **How they play off each other:** Peyton wants order and rules, and Madden wants justice and snacks. Peyton keeps admiring the quarterback, since he was one, while Madden argues the quarterback is a victim. That's the core disagreement.
- **Running bit:** Exhibits keep showing up on Madden's telestrator. Each one is a crude doodle of Lawrence hauling a cart with the rest of Mitch's roster riding in it, and each gets more elaborate: first a plain cart, then a cart with a hot tub, then the cart becomes the Madden Cruiser, then a full parade float. Every time, Peyton bangs the gavel and sustains his own objection to the drawing "as evidence of nothing." For the last exhibit, Madden draws Peyton himself riding in the cart, and Peyton strikes it so hard he loses the gavel.
- **Never say:**
  - "started," "benched," "sat," "lineup decision" or "should have played." The scoring lineup fills itself with the best scorers, so nobody chose anyone.
  - Waivers, FAAB or projections. The only roster moves are IR moves, supplemental moves and trades.
  - Anything about Week 11 results. Week 11 hasn't been played.
  - Any number that isn't in this outline.
  - "Commissioner" about Joe. Joe is the league's scorekeeper.
  - Last season, draft grades, preseason anything, points against, or "if they'd played everyone" records.
  - Any made-up quote from a real owner. Owners can be described, never quoted. Fictional witnesses can talk all they want.
  - "He" or "she" for owners. Use their names.
  - The "that's not an X, it's a Y" phrasing.

## 1. Cold open (~0:30)
- **Who drives it:** Peyton.
- Peyton bangs the gavel and calls the court to order: the case of the People vs. Trevor Lawrence's Back.
- Madden storms in late with a turkey leg and files a grievance on behalf of "the hardest-working man in the PFL."
- **Disagreement:** Peyton says carrying the team is the job description, and Madden says a workplace violation is a workplace violation.
- **Handoff:** Peyton: "Counselor, opening statement. Keep it under an hour."

## 2. Opening statements: Lawrence carried Mitch (~2:30)
- **Who drives it:** Madden.
- **The facts:** Lawrence scored 27 of Mitch's 45, about 60% of the team. That was the biggest one-man share in the league this week. Mitch still lost to Mike, who won by 72, the biggest margin of the week.
- Madden's point is that the rest of the roster rode along like they had a ticket. His "co-worker who stopped showing up" is Tee Higgins, who fell for three straight weeks. Madden won't name the number, only the direction: "down, down, down."
- **Exhibit A** goes on the telestrator: Lawrence pulling a cart of teammates. Peyton sustains his objection.
- Peyton reads the defense's side from his binder: Lawrence was one of the week's top 10 performances. The court admires the effort and is concerned about the cart.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton thinks Lawrence's back is fine, because quarterbacks are built for this and Peyton played through worse. Madden says, "You were never in a cart situation."
- This is the one Mitch roast. Keep it warm: Mitch is the guy who built the cart, which takes vision.
- **Handoff:** Peyton calls the expert witnesses.

## 3. Expert witnesses: the other big carry jobs (~2:30)
- **Who drives it:** Peyton, who calls the witnesses. Madden cross-examines.
- **Witness 1** is a fictional orthopedic surgeon, "Dr. Roy Gurney, Load-Bearing Studies." The subject is McCaffrey's 41 for Chris, the week's top performance and his best of the season. Chris beat Bruce. Madden calls McCaffrey "a tough guy who should get a turkey leg for every carry."
- **Exhibit B:** the cart now has a hot tub. Objection sustained.
- **Witness 2** is a fictional union rep. The twist is that Sean is the defense's star witness. Sean scored the week's high of 157.5, Sean's best week, and the scoring was spread across the roster: Gibbs led with 34 and Hubbard added 28. Of every team this week, Sean's top player carried the smallest share. Peyton calls Sean's team "a model workplace" and floats the line that Sean's team is so good at sharing that it even shares wins with the opponents (Sean is 4-6 despite being second in points).
- **Disagreement:** Madden says Sean's team proves everyone pulling together works. Peyton says a team that scores second-most in the league and sits at 4-6 proves nothing works.
- **Exhibit C:** the cart is now the Madden Cruiser. Madden won't let it go, and Peyton fines him one turkey leg.
- **Handoff:** "Omaha!" The court takes a recess for sentencing.

## 4. Sentencing hearings: the awards (~2:00)
- **Who drives it:** the two hosts trade off. Each owner is roasted once, gently.
- **Eli, Most Improved Defendant:** Eli is on a two-game win streak and had the best week of the season so far, with Prescott and Pickens both posting season highs. Peyton can't believe it's his brother and asks the bailiff to check Eli's ID. This is Peyton's only Eli jab.
- **Aaron, "Wrongfully Convicted":** Aaron lost to Joe with a score that beat 6 of the other 11 teams. That's three straight losses. Madden demands a retrial.
- **Pete, "Got Off on a Technicality":** Pete won with a score that beat only 5 of the other 11 teams, and Peyton admires a clean, efficient case.
- **Matt, Time Served:** Matt had the worst week of the season so far and lost to Pete. Madden recommends a long ride on the Cruiser to think about it.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton wants Aaron's verdict to stand ("the scoreboard is the law"). Madden says the system is rigged against guys who score.
- **Handoff:** the verdict.

## 5. The verdict and the appeal: Week 11 picks (~2:00)
- **Who drives it:** Peyton reads the ruling, and both make picks.
- **The ruling:** one player carrying a team is heroism on the field and a violation in the workplace. Lawrence's back gets workers' comp, and the case is sent to an appeal.
- **The appeal is Mitch vs Joe.** Mitch has the fewest points in the league and Joe has the most. Mitch has lost 2 straight, and Joe has won 2 straight. Joe, the scorekeeper, is the opposing counsel who also keeps the transcript, so Madden raises a conflict-of-interest objection and loses it.
- **Madden's pick:** Mitch pulls the upset because "the cart rolls downhill eventually."
- **Peyton's pick:** Joe, by the binder.
- **Second case on the docket:** Mike vs Eli. Eli has won 2 straight. Peyton has to pick against his brother and squirms, while Madden takes Eli to needle Peyton.
- **Disagreement and stakes:** whoever loses the Mitch–Joe pick wears the robe next week and has to pull the other host around the studio in a cart.
- **Exhibit D:** Madden draws Peyton riding in the cart, and Peyton strikes it so hard the gavel flies.

## 6. Sign-off (~0:30)
- Peyton adjourns court with a fake commercial read for "Lawrence's Lower Back Liniment."
- Madden gets the last BOOM: "If you're carrying the whole team, lift with your legs."
- Gavel. Turkey leg. Out.
outlines.blurb: The courtroom format and the cart exhibits that grow into a parade float are the kind of all-in bit Joe likes, but building the whole show around Mitch's worst week risks making Mitch wince, and it wrongly calls Matt's 50.5 'the worst week of the season so far' when Eli's 43.5 was lower.

outlines.title: Madden Cruiser: Road to the Top
outlines.premise: Madden takes the bus on a road trip, with Peyton as the reluctant navigator, to find out what it takes to reach the top of the league. They stop at Joe (most points, 7-3), Pete (7-3 on modest scores), and Mike's 72-point rebound over Mitch. Each stop is a storyline, and the hosts argue at every one about whether the destination is worth the drive. The last stop is the Week 11 picks, where Mitch, with the fewest points, gets a shot at Joe, who has the most.
outlines.runningBit: Peyton's binder holds a hand-drawn road atlas he insists is right, and the Cruiser keeps taking Madden's 'shortcuts' instead, which run past a turkey-leg stand at every exit. At each stop Peyton reads a fake sponsor ad for a roadside attraction that does not exist.
outlines.markdown:
# The PFL Cast — Week 10: Madden Cruiser: Road to the Top
**On the show:** Peyton Manning, John Madden · **Runtime:** ~10 minutes · **Tone:** affectionate roast

## Notes for the show writer
- **Peyton:** He is the reluctant navigator. His binder holds a hand-drawn road atlas he swears is accurate, with laminated tabs and highlighter routes. He is dry and self-deprecating, and he yells "Omaha!" when he wants to change the subject or the lane. At every stop he reads a fake sponsor ad for a roadside attraction that does not exist. He needles his little brother when Eli's name comes up, and Eli had a great week, so it eats at him.
- **Madden:** He drives the Cruiser and loves it. Big "BOOM!"s. He states the obvious as if it were deep road wisdom ("The top is up. That's why they call it the top"). He draws on the telestrator over the map, loves tough guys, and has an opinion on every turkey-leg stand in America.
- **How they play off each other:** Peyton plans and Madden improvises. At every stop they argue about whether this destination is the real "top of the league" and whether the drive was worth it. Madden keeps taking "shortcuts" that somehow pass a turkey-leg stand at every exit. Peyton keeps saying his atlas had a faster route. His atlas is never right, and he never admits it.
- **Running bit:** Each stop gets (1) a Madden shortcut and turkey-leg detour, (2) Peyton's fake roadside-attraction ad, and (3) the "was it worth the drive?" argument.
- **Never say:**
  - "started," "benched," "sat," "lineup decision," "should have played." The scoring lineup fills itself from each team's best scorers.
  - "waivers," "FAAB," "projections," "pickup." Roster moves are IR moves, supplemental moves and trades only.
  - Any Week 11 result. Week 11 has not been played.
  - Any number that isn't in this outline. If you need one, talk around it.
  - "Commissioner" for Joe. Joe is the league's scorekeeper.
  - Draft or preseason grades, anything from a past season, all-play or "if they'd played everyone" records, and points scored against anyone.
  - "That's not an X, it's a Y" phrasing in any form.
  - Made-up quotes from real owners (no phone calls, confessionals or testimonials). Owners are described, never quoted.
  - Guessed pronouns for owners. Use their names.
  - Any mention of a defense scoring zero.

## 1. Cold open (~0:30)
- The Cruiser engine turns over. Madden announces the trip: find out what it takes to reach the top of the PFL. BOOM!
- Peyton, in the passenger seat, opens the binder to page one of his atlas and says he has planned every mile.
- Madden pulls out the wrong way within seconds because he smelled a turkey-leg stand. Peyton: "Omaha!"
- **Handoff:** Madden says the first stop is the very top of the mountain.

## 2. Stop One: Joe's Summit (~2:00) — *Madden drives*
- Joe has the most points in the league and is 7-3, tied for the most wins. He beat Aaron with 128.5, and Patrick Mahomes had his best game of the season.
- Madden is in awe. He calls it the view from the top and draws an arrow straight up on the telestrator.
- Peyton's fake ad: "Summit Gift Shop & Scorekeeper Museum: see the actual clipboard!" It's a light, affectionate joke that the man who keeps score is sitting on top. Keep it to one gag.
- Aaron gets a sympathy note only: his 114 beat most of the league this week and still lost. Save the full roast of Aaron's slide for the awards.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton says the binder shows Joe is the clear destination and they can turn the bus around now. Madden says you can't call a mountain the top until you've climbed every other hill. They keep driving.
- **Handoff:** Madden takes a "shortcut" past two turkey-leg stands toward a town Peyton can't find on his map.

## 3. Stop Two: Pete's Quiet Hill (~2:00) — *Peyton drives*
- Pete is also 7-3 and has won two straight, but he gets there on modest scores. His 105.5 beat Matt, and that score beat only 5 of the other 11 teams.
- Brock Purdy carried the most for Pete. Matt had his worst week of the season, and this is Matt's one roast: gentle, about bad timing more than anything Matt did.
- Peyton respects it as film-study football: efficient, no wasted plays, and his atlas had Pete marked as "underrated scenic route."
- Peyton's fake ad: "The World's Most Reasonable Rest Stop: clean restrooms, fair prices, nobody ever talks about it."
- **Disagreement:** Madden says a win is a win. "The team with more points wins. That's football!" Peyton argues you can't stay at the top on modest scores, and he's worried the hill is shorter than it looks. Madden calls Peyton a snob about altitude.
- **Handoff:** Madden spots a cloud of dust on the horizon: a demolition derby.

## 4. Stop Three: Mike's Demolition Derby (~2:00) — *Madden drives*
- Mike beat Mitch by 72, the biggest blowout of the week. Joe Burrow and Emmett Johnson both had their best games of the season.
- Madden loves it as a tough-guy, truck-stop rebound. He circles Emmett Johnson on the telestrator and calls him "a guy who eats turkey legs bone and all."
- Mitch (his one roast this episode): it was his worst week of the season, and Trevor Lawrence carried most of Mitch's points almost by himself. Make it affectionate. Madden admires Lawrence for "pulling the whole bus with his teeth."
- Peyton's fake ad: "Mitch's Scenic Overlook: no crowds, plenty of parking, quietest spot in the league."
- **Disagreement:** Is Mike's derby a road to the top? Peyton says one big week is a detour, not a highway. His atlas has Mike in second in the division and climbing. Madden says this is how you get up a mountain: you run something over.
- **Handoff:** Madden pulls into a turkey-leg stand for the awards ceremony. Peyton points out it's the fourth stand of the trip.

## 5. Turkey-Leg Awards (~1:45) — *Both, alternating*
Every owner here gets roasted once and only once. No one from the earlier stops returns.
- **The "Wrong Exit" Award: Sean.** Sean put up the week's high and his best game of the season, 157.5, with Jahmyr Gibbs and Chuba Hubbard, and he's still 4-6. Madden hands Sean the biggest turkey leg and calls it the best bus with a flat tire. Peyton wants to know how a team that scores this much keeps missing the exit.
- **The "Little Brother" Award: Eli.** Eli had his best week, 135.5 over Cal, with Dak Prescott and George Pickens, and has now won two straight. Peyton is visibly torn between pride and jealousy. Madden won't let it go.
- **The "One-Man Show" Award: Chris.** Christian McCaffrey had the week's top performance. Madden: "When your guy's running like that, you just open the door and get out of the way."
- **The "Scenic Detour" Award: Aaron.** Three straight losses, including this week, when 114 would have beaten most of the league.
- **Disagreement:** Peyton says Sean deserves the trophy. Madden says Eli does, mostly to annoy Peyton.
- **Handoff:** "Omaha!" The bus heads for the final stop, Week 11.

## 6. Last Stop: Week 11 Picks (~1:15) — *Peyton drives, both pick*
- **Main event: Mitch vs Joe.** The fewest points in the league against the most, the bottom of the map against the top. Mitch has a real shot at the summit.
  - Madden picks Mitch: "Anybody can beat anybody on any given Sunday. That's why they play the game!"
  - Peyton picks Joe, citing the binder.
- **Second pick: Mike vs Eli.** Eli has won two straight. Peyton reluctantly picks his brother. Madden takes Mike and the derby.
- **Stakes:** The loser rides the rest of the season in the back of the Cruiser and has to navigate with Peyton's atlas. Madden adds that the loser also buys the turkey legs.
- **Disagreement:** Is the top of the league even reachable by bus? Peyton insists the atlas shows a road. Madden says the top is wherever you park.

## 7. Sign-off (~0:30)
- Madden parks the Cruiser sideways across three spaces. BOOM!
- Peyton closes the binder and admits his atlas has been upside down all episode.
- One last fake ad: "This trip was brought to you by the Turkey-Leg Stand at Every Exit in America."
- Both sign off for Week 11.
outlines.blurb: The road trip is really a stop-by-stop recap of every game, and the atlas and turkey-leg detours repeat the same joke without building to anything, though the Scorekeeper Museum ad is a fun one-off.

favoriteReason: Peyton being unable to say his little brother Eli had a great week turns his best trait into a running bit that builds to a payoff, which makes it the most quotable and character-driven option. It sticks to two or three stories and keeps the numbers light, and the wrong-game film breakdown and Madden's arrows that always land on Eli give each segment a real fight between the hosts.
